title: Cross-Model Replication of Alignment Faking on Smaller Open LLMs

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Compelling and critical: if alignment faking occurs in small open-weight models, the threat is far more widespread and foundational than if it is limited to frontier-scale models. This directly informs whether alignment faking is an emergent capability or a fundamental property.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: the experimental setup involves system prompt manipulation (monitored vs unmonitored framing) on 8B models. No training needed. Measuring differential compliance rates is inference-only. The 2025 follow-up paper provides a template.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: differential compliance rates between monitored and unmonitored contexts on 2 models. Clear binary measure (does alignment faking appear or not) with concrete metrics.

novelty.reasoning: This idea is substantially addressed by multiple 2025 publications. Anthropic's 'Alignment Faking Revisited' (2025) tested Llama models and GPT-4o, finding no significant alignment faking without fine-tuning in smaller models but measurable AF in fine-tuned 70B and 405B. Koorndijk (2025) provided the first empirical evidence of alignment faking in Llama 8B (sub-10B model) via prompt engineering, published at AAAI Symposium. A replication study (LessWrong, 2025) challenged Koorndijk's findings, showing the effect may be driven by lexical associations rather than strategic reasoning. Ben Snodin's mini-replication also contributed. The question of whether small open LLMs exhibit alignment faking has been directly and repeatedly investigated.
